ai.description: *Hoplobatrachus litoralis* is a large frog reaching 10 cm. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal spots, a pale vertebral stripe, and a pointed snout. Distinctive features include a white belly and webbed toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hoplobatrachus litoralis* is uniquely distinguished by its distinctively pointed snout and the absence of a mid-dorsal vertebral stripe, unlike the common *H. tigerinus*.
ai.habitat: *Hoplobatrachus litoralis* inhabits low-lying coastal areas and freshwater wetlands, typically found in mangrove-associated vegetation at elevations near sea level.
ai.behavior: The Bangladesh Coastal Bullfrog is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively hunt insects and small vertebrates near coastal wetlands and agricultural fields.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hoplobatrachus litoralis* is an explosive breeder that lays large clutches of eggs in temporary monsoon pools. Breeding occurs primarily during the rainy season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hoplobatrachus litoralis* is endemic to the coastal regions of Bangladesh, specifically occurring in the low-lying Chittagong and Cox’s Bazar districts.
ai.callDescription: The Bangladesh Coastal Bullfrog produces a low-pitched, rhythmic "gurgling" croak, typically heard during the monsoon season in coastal wetlands and brackish water habitats.
